![](/content/exams/anzca/1999/B/8/standard-image30.png){fig-alt="Superimposed aortic root and radial artery pressure waveforms against time"}

Red line = aortic root 

Blue line = radial artery

**Key differences**

1.  **radial has delayed peak relative to aortic**
    Pressure wave takes time to propagate through vessels resulting in observed delay 

    Stiffer vessels (e.g. with ageing or vascular disease) → faster pressure wave propagation → less delay
2.  **radial has delayed and smoother dicrotic notch**
    Dicrotic notch of aortic waveform is sharp and is related to the sudden closure of aortic valve
3.  **radial has steeper, higher and narrower systolic component and lower diastolic pressures than aortic**
    Aorta is more compliant than peripheral vasculature → Radial has less elastic tissue and reduced windkessel effect, Radial and aortic mean arterial pressures (MAP) are relatively similar radial usually slightly lower
